questions.prompt: Find the standard matrix of \(T:\mathbb R^2 \to \mathbb R^2\) defined by \(T(x, y)=(2x-y,3y)\).
questions.answer: The columns of the standard matrix are \(T(e_1)\) and \(T(e_2)\). \(T(1,0)=(2,0)\), and \(T(0,1)=(-1,3)\). Therefore the standard matrix is \(\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\0&3\end{pmatrix}\).

questions.prompt: Find the standard matrix of \(T:\mathbb R^3 \to \mathbb R^2\) defined by \(T(x,y,z)=(x+z,2y-z)\).
questions.answer: Use the standard basis vectors of \(\mathbb R^3\). \(T(1,0,0)=(1,0)\), \(T(0,1,0)=(0,2)\), and \(T(0,0,1)=(1,-1)\). These output vectors are the columns of the matrix. Therefore the matrix is \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&1\\0&2&-1\end{pmatrix}\).

questions.prompt: A linear map \(T:\mathbb R^2 \to \mathbb R^3\) satisfies \(T(1,0)=(1,2,0)\) and \(T(0,1)=(-1,0,3)\). Find its standard matrix.
questions.answer: For a standard matrix, the first column is \(T(1,0)\) and the second column is \(T(0,1)\). Therefore the matrix is \(\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\2&0\\0&3\end{pmatrix}\).
Multiply the matrix by the column vector \((4,5)\). The first component is \(2\cdot4+(-1)\cdot5=8-5=3\). The second component is \(0\cdot4+3\cdot5=15\). Therefore \(T(4,5)=(3,15)\).

questions.prompt: Find the matrix of \(D:P_2 \to P_1\), \(D(p)=p'\), using domain basis \((1,x,x^2)\) and codomain basis \((1,x)\).
questions.answer: Apply \(D\) to the domain basis. \(D(1)=0\), with coordinates \((0,0)\) in \((1,x)\). \(D(x)=1\), with coordinates \((1,0)\). \(D(x^2)=2x\), with coordinates \((0,2)\). These coordinate vectors are the columns. Therefore the matrix is \(\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\0&0&2\end{pmatrix}\).

questions.prompt: Find the matrix of \(E:P_2 \to \mathbb R\), \(E(p)=p(0)\), using basis \((1,x,x^2)\) for \(P_2\) and the standard basis for \(\mathbb R\).
questions.answer: Evaluate each basis polynomial at 0. \(E(1)=1\), \(E(x)=0\), and \(E(x^2)=0\). Since the codomain \(\mathbb R\) has one coordinate, these become columns \([1]\), \([0]\), and \([0]\). Therefore the matrix is \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\end{pmatrix}\).

questions.prompt: For \(T:\mathbb R^2 \to \mathbb R^2\) with matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}\), find \(T(e_1)\) and \(T(e_2)\).
questions.answer: The columns of the standard matrix are the images of the standard basis vectors. The first column is \((1,3)\), so \(T(e_1)=(1,3)\). The second column is \((2,4)\), so \(T(e_2)=(2,4)\).

questions.prompt: Find the standard matrix of the projection \(T:\mathbb R^3 \to \mathbb R^3\) defined by \(T(x,y,z)=(x,y,0)\).
questions.answer: Compute images of the standard basis. \(T(1,0,0)=(1,0,0)\), \(T(0,1,0)=(0,1,0)\), and \(T(0,0,1)=(0,0,0)\). These are the columns. Therefore the standard matrix is \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}\).

questions.prompt: A matrix representation [T] has size \(3\times 2\). What are the dimensions of the domain and codomain if standard coordinates are used?
questions.answer: A matrix with size m by n represents a map from \(\mathbb R^n\) to \(\mathbb R^m\) in standard coordinates. A \(3\times 2\) matrix has 2 input coordinates and 3 output coordinates. Therefore the domain is \(\mathbb R^2\) and the codomain is \(\mathbb R^3\).

questions.prompt: A learner puts \(T(e_1)\) and \(T(e_2)\) as rows instead of columns when building a standard matrix. Diagnose the error.
questions.answer: Matrix multiplication forms a linear combination of the columns using the input coordinates. For input \((a,b)\), the product \(A(a,b)\) equals a times column 1 plus b times column 2. To get \(T(ae_1+be_2)=aT(e_1)+bT(e_2)\), column 1 must be \(T(e_1)\) and column 2 must be \(T(e_2)\). Putting them as rows generally represents a different map.
